title: Constructivism
definition: Learners build understanding by connecting new experiences to what they already know, rather than receiving knowledge passively.
classroom: Start with a hands-on task using local materials, then let learners explain what they noticed before you name the concept. In Ghanaian classrooms this works well with counting stones, bottle caps and market role-play.

title: Zone of Proximal Development
definition: The space between what a learner can do alone and what they can do with support — the target zone for instruction.
classroom: Pair a stronger learner with a learner who needs support on the same task, and withdraw your own help as they succeed ('scaffolding').

title: Concrete–Pictorial–Abstract
definition: Understanding deepens when a concept is met first with real objects, then pictures, then symbols.
classroom: For fractions: cut real oranges, then draw the fractions, and only then write 1/2 + 1/4.

title: Formative assessment
definition: Assessment used during learning to adapt teaching, rather than only at the end to grade it.
classroom: Replace hands-up questioning with mini-whiteboards or a quick exit slip so every learner answers, and you can see who to reteach tomorrow.

title: Growth mindset
definition: Learners who believe ability grows with effort persist longer than those who believe ability is fixed.
classroom: Praise the method and the effort ('you tried three ways to solve it'), not the child's cleverness.

title: Cognitive load theory
definition: Working memory is small; instruction must reduce extraneous load to leave room for learning.
classroom: Give one instruction at a time, use worked examples first, and avoid decorating slides with material that competes with the content.
